Twelve growth ideas ranked for Arata
Answers to the six questions buyers keep asking

statHint.statLabel: ASKED AGAIN AND AGAIN, UNANSWERED ON SITE

adapt: Build this move from the listening lines (listen.*), not from the skill's generic examples. Pick the 4 to 8 questions and doubts that recur across listen.theme lines (highest count first, rising week on week first among equals) and check each against the site, the policies and the catalogue in the ledger: answered clearly, answered but hidden, or not answered. For every unanswered or hidden one, write the finished answer for three surfaces: a PDP block next to the buy button, an FAQ entry in the buyer's own words, and a one-line ad or email angle. Quote the real people who asked (listen.quote lines only, with their links) and give the count behind each question. Never answer with a claim the ledger does not back: write "to confirm with the brand" instead.

discipline: Ad Angles From What People Say
titleHint: Twelve ad angles in your buyers' own words
adapt: Turn the listening themes into ad angles. For each angle name the theme it comes from (listen.theme line: count, sentiment split, week-on-week change), the exact phrase people used (listen.quote lines only, linked), the objection or desire it answers, and the hook, primary text and headline in that language. Praise themes become proof angles, complaint themes about rivals become switch angles, recurring questions become objection-handling angles. Rank by mentions and momentum. Keep the brand's claims inside the ledger. No disclaimers or 'illustrative' labels on the ads.

discipline: Social Posts From What Was Heard
titleHint: Posts, carousels and replies from what people asked

statHint.statLabel: BUILT FROM REAL QUESTIONS AND PRAISE

adapt: Write a two-week slate of organic posts built only from what Brew heard: recurring questions become answer posts and carousels, praise becomes proof posts, live threads become replies. Do it per platform the brand is on or should be on (Instagram, TikTok, YouTube Shorts, X, LinkedIn, Pinterest, Reddit, Quora, Facebook groups), in each platform's native format and length. For every post cite the listen.theme line (count, sentiment, week-on-week) and, when you quote a person, the listen.quote line with its link. Replies in communities are written as a person from the brand, say so where the community requires it, and follow that community's rules; Brew drafts, the team posts.

titleHint: The one question to ask in r/<community> this week

statHint.statLabel: WHAT WE STILL DO NOT KNOW

adapt: From the full evidence, find what Brew still does not know that changes a decision (a gap between what the brand claims and what people say, a theme with many questions and no answer, a rival switch reason we cannot explain). Pick ONE question per community, name 2 to 4 real communities from the listening data (listen.community or the subreddits in listen.quote links) where it fits, quote their posting rules as 'to check' when not in the evidence, and write the draft post in each community's style, disclosing the brand affiliation where the rules require it. Set the reply threshold (how many useful replies before we act, usually 5 to 15) and say exactly which moves the replies will turn into once the threshold is met. Brew never posts; the team does, from a real account.

titleHint: The next 90 days of events, planned backwards

statHint.statLabel: IN THE BRAND'S MARKETS, NEXT 90 DAYS

adapt: Use only the events in the calendar lines (cal.*) that are relevant to the brand's markets and category; never add a festival the brand does not sell into. For each event plan backwards from the event date: creative ready, offer decided, stock checked, ads live, emails and WhatsApp scheduled, and the day after. Give dates, owners and the budget split. Say what last year's same window looked like when the ledger has it, or that it is to be pulled. Measure each event against the same window last year.

titleHint: When it turns cold in Delhi, the ads switch on
adapt: Only if the weather lines (pulse weather) show a link between the brand's products and the weather (cold, heat, rain, pollution, humidity) in its top cities. Write 2 to 4 standing rules: the signal and its threshold, the cities, what switches on (ad sets, creative, email/WhatsApp, homepage banner), what switches off, the spend cap, and the hold-out share so we can measure the lift. Cite the forecast lines with their dates. If the evidence shows no weather link, say so and write the rules as hypotheses to test small.

titleHint: Winning the people who gave a rival two stars

statHint.statLabel: RIVAL REVIEWS AND AD COMMENTS READ

adapt: Build from rival 1 to 3 star reviews and complaints in rival ad comments (rival-weakness and listen lines where about = rival). Group the complaints into themes with counts, check whether the brand really does better on each (ledger evidence only), and write the switch moves: comparison page sections, ads aimed at the rival's unhappy buyers (no rival trademarks in ad text where the platform forbids it), and replies in threads where people are asking for alternatives. Quote only real linked reviews. Never state why a rival does something; never say a rival lacks something, say 'not observed'.

discipline: AI Search From Fixed Buyer Questions
titleHint: Being named when buyers ask AI which to buy

statHint.statLabel: AI ANSWERS THAT NAME THE BRAND

adapt: Use the fixed set of buyer questions Brew asks the AI assistants every week (ai.* ledger and ai-seo pulse lines): which answers name the brand, which name rivals, which sources they cite. Add the questions people really ask from the listening lines. For each question we lose, write the answer asset that would get cited (an FAQ block, a comparison table, a facts page, a third-party listing to get on) and where it lives. Measure on the same questions, asked the same way every week.

discipline: Creator Seeding From People Already Posting
titleHint: Seeding the twelve people already talking about you
adapt: Start from people already posting about the brand or its category (creator lines and the authors of listen items with real reach), not from a cold creator search. For each, cite what they posted (linked), their audience fit, and the ask: gift only, gift plus brief, or paid. Write the outreach message, the seeding brief and the code/link scheme so orders can be counted. Paid partnerships carry the platform's partnership label. Claims stay inside the ledger.

titleHint: The first three seconds that work in your category

statHint.statLabel: READ FROM TOP VIDEOS IN THE CATEGORY

adapt: Use the video read lines (video.*: hook, scenes, format, length, the views where given) from the brand's own, rivals' and category videos, and the viral ones (a line saying viral, Nx the creator's usual views). Name the patterns that recur in the strongest ones, then write 6 to 10 hooks and two full scripts for the brand in those patterns, each tied to the video line it learns from. Do not copy a video; learn its structure. Cite views and dates only as the lines give them.

discipline: Price And Offer From Shopping Position
titleHint: Where the price sits on the shelf people compare

statHint.statLabel: PRICE RANK ON THE SHOPPING SHELF

adapt: Use the shopping and marketplace position lines (price-offer pulse lines: Google Shopping and Amazon prices, rank, ratings, offers seen) for the brand's hero products against what sits next to them. Say where each hero ranks on price, on rating and on offer, and what a buyer sees side by side. Recommend at most three price or offer moves with margin math from the ledger, and the guard (margin floor) that stops them. Discounts are a last resort; prefer bundles, guarantees and value framing when the evidence supports them.

discipline: Review And Complaint Fix From Listening
titleHint: Fixing the sizing complaint people keep repeating
adapt: Take the top one or two complaint themes in the listening lines (listen.theme with the most negative mentions, and rising week on week). Show the count, the negative share and the trend, quote 3 to 5 linked real complaints, and trace the cause where the evidence allows (product, sizing, delivery, expectation set by the site or ads). Write the fix for each surface Brew can touch (PDP copy, size guide, FAQ, post-purchase message, ad promise) and the brief for what only the brand can fix (product, ops). Then the reply the brand posts where people complained, and how we tell people it is fixed. Measure the complaint's share of mentions, 30 and 60 days on.

titleHint: The searches rising this month in your category
adapt: Use the search pulse lines (seo: keyword volumes, trends, autocomplete, keyword gaps against rivals) to find the 5 to 10 searches rising or uncovered in the brand's market. For each, the page or content piece to make, the angle from the listening lines (what people say around that search), and where it links. Cite volumes and changes only as the lines give them.

titleHint: Six rules that run while the team sleeps
adapt: Write 4 to 8 standing rules Brew can run once the brand approves them: the signal (a listening theme spiking, a weather threshold, stock running low, a rival price change, a reorder day reached, a festival plan point), the threshold, the action on the brand's own stack (email, WhatsApp, an ad set on or off, a banner), the cap, and the hold-out share. Each rule names the evidence line that would fire it and how often it would have fired recently if the lines show it. Brew sends only email and WhatsApp itself; everything else runs on the brand's connected accounts.

discipline: Emails That Answer What People Ask
titleHint: The five emails your buyers asked for
adapt: Write the emails and WhatsApp messages that answer the questions and doubts people raise most in the listening lines, timed to when a buyer has them (before the first order, after delivery, at the reorder point). Each message cites the theme and count it answers and quotes a linked real question where it helps. Subject lines, preview text, body and the one button. Hold out a share of the list so we know the lift.
